findings.note: src/canon.rs evaluate_claim: qualitative forces value_derived/unit_derived false, so a statement deriving 0.2 s with authored value: present, unit: none, operator: EQ yields zero flags (unit omission hidden); the value part is a documented stray-number choice but the unit suppression is not.
unit_derived = !qualitative && ...: in the qualitative-on-measurable test the parse derives s, author wrote none, and unit_check is Ok rather than Omission; the four-case table says that is a flag.
tests/parity_annotations.rs:444-452 runs canon --fill with cwd = CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, the real corpus, concurrently with the read-only corpus tests.

classify_slot maps (false,true) to Annotation unconditionally and a numeric authored triple is not qualitative, so an authored LE/0.2/s the parse does not derive is no longer flagged (old authored_is_num gate did flag it).
tests/parity_annotations.rs:328 contains("ann") is a loose substring check on the REQ-0001 row; true but low consequence.
value_unit_cell returns at the first FLAG or 'ann value' branch, dropping a concurrent unit annotation from the cell.
authored_is_numeric checks only the first char (same as the old gate); a digit-leading state name is an unlikely edge case.
No test in parity_annotations.rs drives unit_check to Contradiction/Omission or op_check to Omission; only value and op contradiction are covered.
Same as F03: fill_accepts_the_corpus_that_only_annotates calls corpus(['canon','--fill']) on the checkout, and nothing proves no write happened.
value_unit_cell lines ~1756-1761: both value and unit Annotation renders only 'ann value', so the unit annotation is invisible in the row.
Same as F04 with a concrete trigger: a numeric authored triple on a statement with no quantity becomes three annotations, zero flags, and --fill accepts it.
